learningObjective: State the online softmax update rules that let a single-pass streaming algorithm compute exact softmax over a partitioned row.
stem: An online softmax algorithm streams over a row in tiles B_1, B_2, .... After processing tile B_t it maintains a running max m_t and a running denominator d_t such that d_t = sum_{i in B_1..t} exp(x_i - m_t). Which update rule is correct when a new tile B_{t+1} arrives with local max m' and local denominator d' = sum_{i in B_{t+1}} exp(x_i - m')?
codeSnippet:
# State after tile t:  m_t (running max), d_t = sum_{i<=t} exp(x_i - m_t)
# New tile stats:      m' = max over B_{t+1};   d' = sum_{i in B_{t+1}} exp(x_i - m')
# We want:             m_{t+1} = max(m_t, m'),  d_{t+1} = sum_{i<=t+1} exp(x_i - m_{t+1})

options.text: m_{t+1} = max(m_t, m') ; d_{t+1} = d_t * exp(m_t - m_{t+1}) + d' * exp(m' - m_{t+1})  (both partial denominators are rescaled by the exponential of the difference between their old reference max and the new global max.)
m_{t+1} = max(m_t, m') ; d_{t+1} = d_t + d'  (the max is the elementwise maximum; the denominator combines by simple addition because both partial sums are already normalized.)

m_{t+1} = max(m_t, m') ; d_{t+1} = d_t + d' * exp(m' - m_{t+1})  (only the new tile's denominator needs a correction factor because the old running sum was already normalized to the true maximum seen so far.)
m_{t+1} = m_t + m' ; d_{t+1} = d_t + d'  (sum both running max and denominator to preserve the streaming invariant.)

explanation: d_t was accumulated with reference max m_t. If m_{t+1} > m_t, every term in d_t must be re-referenced: exp(x_i - m_t) = exp(x_i - m_{t+1}) * exp(m_{t+1} - m_t)^{-1}, so d_t is rescaled by exp(m_t - m_{t+1}) (which is <= 1). Symmetrically d' is rescaled by exp(m' - m_{t+1}). Summing gives the correct d_{t+1} = sum_{i<=t+1} exp(x_i - m_{t+1}). This is the identity that lets FlashAttention (and any tiled softmax) work in a single pass with exact results.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: both partial denominators are rescaled to the new global max.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: without rescaling, the sums use different reference maxes and are incomparable.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: only rescaling the new tile leaves the old sum on a stale reference; the old d_t also needs a rescale unless m_t is already the new global max.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: max is not additive; adding running maxes yields nonsense.

assumptions: All exp arguments (x_i - m_{t+1}) are non-positive so no overflow.
nonImplications: Does not imply that online softmax is faster than a two-pass safe softmax on all hardware; it is faster mainly when reloading the row would be expensive (attention).
Does not imply that the algorithm avoids all rounding differences from summation order.
